Docker.title: Containerise one of your existing projects
Docker.description: Take a project that currently runs only on your laptop and make it start with one command on any machine.
acceptance_criteria: A Dockerfile builds the project with no manual steps after the build
The image runs with a single docker run command and the README shows it
Image size is under 500 MB and the README says how you got there

Kubernetes.title: Deploy a two service app to a local cluster
Kubernetes.description: Run an API and a database on minikube or kind, with the manifests kept in the repository.
acceptance_criteria: Deployment, Service and ConfigMap manifests are committed
The app survives deleting a pod, and the README shows the recovery
Resource requests and limits are set and justified in the README

Terraform.title: Provision your project infrastructure as code
Terraform.description: Replace console clicking with Terraform for the resources your project needs.
acceptance_criteria: terraform apply creates the resources from scratch on an empty account
State handling and variables are explained in the README
terraform destroy leaves nothing behind, verified and noted

CI/CD.title: Add a pipeline that blocks broken code
CI/CD.description: Wire your repository so tests and a build run on every push before anything can merge.
acceptance_criteria: The pipeline runs install, lint, test and build on every push
A deliberately broken commit fails the pipeline, with the run linked in the README
The badge or run link is visible in the README

GitHub Actions.title: Automate tests and release with Actions
GitHub Actions.description: Write a workflow that checks every push and publishes an artefact on a tag.
acceptance_criteria: A workflow file runs the test suite on pull requests
A second job builds and uploads an artefact on tagged commits
Secrets are used through repository secrets, never committed

Jenkins.title: Build a declarative Jenkins pipeline
Jenkins.description: Set up a Jenkinsfile that builds, tests and archives one of your projects.
acceptance_criteria: The Jenkinsfile defines build, test and archive stages
The pipeline runs on a local Jenkins instance and the README shows the stage view
A failing test stops the pipeline before the archive stage

Ansible.title: Configure a server with a playbook
Ansible.description: Turn manual server setup into a repeatable playbook.
acceptance_criteria: A playbook installs and configures the service from a clean machine
Running the playbook twice changes nothing the second time
Inventory and variables are separated from the tasks

Monitoring.title: Instrument a service and watch it
Monitoring.description: Add metrics and alerts to an API you already have, so you can tell when it is unhealthy.
acceptance_criteria: The service exposes request count, error rate and latency metrics
A dashboard shows those three signals over time
One alert rule fires on a simulated failure, with a screenshot in the README

Prometheus.title: Export and query your own metrics
Prometheus.description: Expose application metrics and answer real questions with PromQL.
acceptance_criteria: The app exposes a /metrics endpoint scraped by Prometheus
Three PromQL queries answering real questions are documented
A recording rule or alert rule is defined and explained

Grafana.title: Build a dashboard someone else could read
Grafana.description: Turn raw metrics into a dashboard that shows health at a glance.
acceptance_criteria: The dashboard has panels for traffic, errors and latency
The dashboard JSON is committed to the repository
The README explains what a healthy and an unhealthy board looks like

Nginx.title: Put a reverse proxy in front of your app
Nginx.description: Serve your application through nginx with TLS and sensible caching.
acceptance_criteria: nginx proxies to the app and the config is in the repository
Static assets are served with cache headers that the README explains
HTTPS works locally with a self signed certificate and the steps are documented

Networking.title: Map and debug your own stack's network path
Networking.description: Document how a request reaches your app and prove you can debug each hop.
acceptance_criteria: A diagram shows DNS, TLS, load balancer and app for your deployed project
Commands used to debug each hop are recorded with their output
One deliberate misconfiguration is diagnosed and fixed in the write up

Shell scripting.title: Automate a task you repeat every week
Shell scripting.description: Replace a manual routine with a script that is safe to run twice.
acceptance_criteria: The script handles failure with set -euo pipefail and clear messages
It takes arguments and prints usage when called wrong
The README shows a real run with its output

Linux.title: Run your project on a Linux server you manage
Linux.description: Deploy to a plain virtual machine and keep it running without a platform doing it for you.
acceptance_criteria: The service runs under systemd and restarts after a reboot
Logs go to journald and the README shows how to read them
A non root user owns the process and file permissions are explained

Infrastructure as code.title: Rebuild your environment from a fresh clone
Infrastructure as code.description: Make the whole environment reproducible from code, with no undocumented steps.
acceptance_criteria: Every resource the project needs is defined in code
A second environment can be created by changing variables only
The README lists the exact commands from clone to running system

Cloud fundamentals.title: Deploy one project to a cloud provider end to end
Cloud fundamentals.description: Take a working project and run it on cloud infrastructure you configured yourself.
acceptance_criteria: The app is reachable on a public URL created by you
Compute, storage and networking choices are justified in the README
Monthly cost is estimated and written down

AWS.title: Run a project on AWS with storage and compute
AWS.description: Use at least two AWS services together and explain the wiring.
acceptance_criteria: The app runs on EC2, Lambda or ECS and is reachable
Files or artefacts are stored in S3 through the SDK
IAM permissions are least privilege and explained in the README

Azure.title: Deploy a project to Azure with managed services
Azure.description: Use Azure compute plus one managed service and document the setup.
acceptance_criteria: The app is deployed and reachable on an Azure endpoint
One managed service, such as storage or a database, is wired in
Configuration is kept out of code using app settings

GCP.title: Ship a project on Google Cloud
GCP.description: Deploy a container and connect one managed Google Cloud service.
acceptance_criteria: The container runs on Cloud Run or GKE with a working URL
A managed service such as Cloud Storage or BigQuery is used
The README shows the deploy command and the cost estimate

SQL.title: Answer five real questions with SQL
SQL.description: Load a public dataset into Postgres and answer questions that need joins and windows.
acceptance_criteria: Schema and load scripts are committed and run from scratch
Five queries with joins, grouping and at least one window function are documented
Each query has its result and a one line explanation of what it answers

PostgreSQL.title: Design and tune a small Postgres schema
PostgreSQL.description: Model a real domain properly and prove your indexes do something.
acceptance_criteria: Tables, keys and constraints are created by a migration file
EXPLAIN output before and after an index is shown in the README
A transaction demonstrates correct behaviour under concurrent updates

MySQL.title: Build a normalised MySQL database for a real domain
MySQL.description: Model a small system, load data and show the queries that run against it.
acceptance_criteria: The schema is created by a committed SQL file with keys and constraints
Sample data loads with one command
Five queries answering real questions are documented with output

MongoDB.title: Model a document heavy feature in MongoDB
MongoDB.description: Choose embedding or referencing deliberately and justify the choice with queries.
acceptance_criteria: Collections and indexes are created by a committed script
The README explains where you embedded and where you referenced, and why
An aggregation pipeline answers one real question

Redis.title: Add caching to a slow endpoint
Redis.description: Find a genuinely slow path in your app and put Redis in front of it.
acceptance_criteria: Latency before and after is measured and recorded in the README
Cache keys and expiry are documented, including how stale data is avoided
The app still works correctly when Redis is unavailable

REST APIs.title: Design and document an API someone else could use
REST APIs.description: Build a small API with the details that matter: status codes, validation, pagination.
acceptance_criteria: Every endpoint validates input and returns a consistent error shape
List endpoints are paginated and the contract is documented
An OpenAPI file or a Postman collection is committed

Authentication.title: Add real authentication to one of your projects
Authentication.description: Implement sign up, sign in and protected routes without copying an entire template.
acceptance_criteria: Passwords are hashed with bcrypt or argon2, never stored in plain text
Sessions or tokens expire and the expiry behaviour is tested
Protected routes reject missing and tampered credentials, shown by tests

System design.title: Write a design document for your own project at scale
System design.description: Take a project you built and explain how it would survive a hundred times the traffic.
acceptance_criteria: A diagram shows components, data flow and the bottleneck you identified
Two design options are compared with their tradeoffs
Capacity numbers are estimated rather than guessed, with the working shown

Caching.title: Add a cache layer and prove it helps
Caching.description: Measure first, cache second, and show the difference.
acceptance_criteria: Baseline latency and load are measured before any caching
Cache invalidation rules are written down and demonstrated
The README shows the measured improvement and the correctness risk you accepted

Message queues.title: Move slow work off the request path
Message queues.description: Introduce a queue so a slow task stops blocking the user.
acceptance_criteria: A producer and a consumer run as separate processes
A failed job is retried and eventually lands in a dead letter path
The README shows the before and after request timing

Microservices.title: Split one feature out into its own service
Microservices.description: Take a module out of a monolith and make it communicate over the network.
acceptance_criteria: Two services run independently and communicate over HTTP or a queue
Each service has its own data and the boundary is explained
The README is honest about what the split made harder

Testing.title: Bring one project from no tests to a meaningful suite
Testing.description: Write tests that would actually catch a regression, not tests that restate the code.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover the core logic including edge cases
One integration test exercises the real path end to end
The README shows a bug the suite caught, with the failing output

Jest.title: Test a front end feature properly
Jest.description: Cover a component with tests that survive a refactor.
acceptance_criteria: Tests exercise behaviour through the rendered output, not internals
Async states, loading and error, are both covered
The suite runs in CI on every push

Playwright.title: Automate the critical path of your app
Playwright.description: Write end to end tests for the flow that must never break.
acceptance_criteria: One spec covers the full sign in to main action journey
Tests run headless in CI and produce a trace on failure
Flakiness is addressed with waiting on state, not fixed timeouts

Python.title: Turn a notebook into a package someone can install
Python.description: Take analysis code out of a notebook and make it reusable and testable.
acceptance_criteria: Code is organised into modules with functions that take arguments
Tests cover the core functions including one edge case
The README shows installing and running it in three commands

Pandas.title: Clean a messy public dataset end to end
Pandas.description: Pick a genuinely dirty dataset and document every decision you made about it.
acceptance_criteria: Every cleaning step is a function with a comment on why it is needed
Missing values and duplicates are handled with a stated rule
Before and after row counts and column types are shown in the README

NumPy.title: Rewrite a slow loop as array operations
NumPy.description: Take working but slow numeric code and vectorise it.
acceptance_criteria: The loop version and the array version both exist and produce identical output
Timing for both is recorded in the README
The explanation says which NumPy behaviour made the difference

scikit-learn.title: Build an honest model pipeline
scikit-learn.description: Train a model where the validation number can be trusted.
acceptance_criteria: Preprocessing sits inside a Pipeline so nothing leaks across the split
Cross validation scores are reported with their spread, not one lucky number
A baseline model is included so the improvement is measurable

Machine learning.title: Ship a model with an honest evaluation
Machine learning.description: Train, evaluate and write up a model as if a reviewer would question every number.
acceptance_criteria: A baseline and the trained model are compared on the same held out split
The metric matches the problem and the README says why that metric
One failure mode of the model is documented with examples

Deep learning.title: Train a small network and show the training curve
Deep learning.description: Build and train a network from scratch rather than only calling a pretrained one.
acceptance_criteria: The model definition and training loop are your own code
Training and validation curves are plotted and read in the README
One overfitting fix is applied and its effect is shown

PyTorch.title: Write a training loop you fully understand
PyTorch.description: Implement dataset, model and loop without a high level trainer.
acceptance_criteria: A custom Dataset and DataLoader feed the model
The training loop shows forward, loss, backward and step explicitly
Checkpoints are saved and a saved model is reloaded for inference

TensorFlow.title: Train and export a model for serving
TensorFlow.description: Go from training to a saved model that something else can load.
acceptance_criteria: The model is trained with a validation split and callbacks
The model is exported in SavedModel format and loaded again in a separate script
Inference on a single example is demonstrated end to end

NLP.title: Build a text classifier and inspect its mistakes
NLP.description: Classify real text and spend as much time on the errors as on the accuracy.
acceptance_criteria: Preprocessing steps are documented with their effect on the score
A confusion matrix and ten real misclassified examples are discussed
A baseline such as majority class or TF-IDF is included for comparison

Computer vision.title: Build an image pipeline with real preprocessing
Computer vision.description: Work with images end to end, including the unglamorous preparation.
acceptance_criteria: Loading, resizing and augmentation are implemented and shown visually
The model is evaluated on a held out set with per class results
Three failure cases are shown with an explanation of why they fail

Statistics.title: Answer a question with a test, not a vibe
Statistics.description: Take a real question about a dataset and answer it with a stated method.
acceptance_criteria: The hypothesis and the test chosen are written down before the result
Assumptions of the test are checked and reported
The conclusion states the effect size, not only the p value

Feature engineering.title: Show that your features earn their place
Feature engineering.description: Create features deliberately and measure whether each one helps.
acceptance_criteria: At least five engineered features are documented with their reasoning
Model performance with and without each group of features is compared
Leakage is explicitly checked for and the check is shown

Data cleaning.title: Publish a reproducible cleaning pipeline
Data cleaning.description: Turn a raw file into an analysis ready table with one command.
acceptance_criteria: One script takes the raw file and writes the cleaned file
Every rule, such as dropping or imputing, is justified in a comment
A data quality report of row counts and null counts is produced

Data visualisation.title: Build a chart set that answers a question
Data visualisation.description: Make three charts that together tell one story, with no decoration for its own sake.
acceptance_criteria: Each chart answers a stated question in its caption
Axes, units and sources are labelled on every chart
The README says which chart type you rejected and why

Model deployment.title: Serve your model behind an API
Model deployment.description: Move a trained model out of the notebook and into something callable.
acceptance_criteria: A POST endpoint accepts JSON input and returns a prediction with the model version
The model is loaded once at startup, not per request
The README shows a curl call and the measured response time

MLflow.title: Track your experiments so results are reproducible
MLflow.description: Stop losing runs and start comparing them properly.
acceptance_criteria: Parameters, metrics and artefacts are logged for every run
Two runs are compared in the UI with a screenshot in the README
A logged model is loaded back and used for inference

Jupyter.title: Turn a notebook into a readable analysis
Jupyter.description: Make a notebook that someone else can run top to bottom and follow.
acceptance_criteria: The notebook runs from a clean kernel with no hidden state
Markdown cells explain each step and the conclusion
Heavy functions are imported from a module rather than pasted in cells

ETL.title: Build a pipeline that loads data on a schedule
ETL.description: Extract from a source, transform it and load it somewhere queryable.
acceptance_criteria: The pipeline is idempotent: running it twice does not duplicate rows
Failures are logged and the run can be resumed
A schedule is configured and documented

Data modelling.title: Design a reporting schema for a real domain
Data modelling.description: Build a model that answers business questions without contortions.
acceptance_criteria: Fact and dimension tables are defined with a stated grain
Three business questions are answered with queries against the model
The README explains what you denormalised and why

A/B testing.title: Design and analyse one experiment properly
A/B testing.description: Run an experiment on a real or simulated dataset and report it honestly.
acceptance_criteria: Sample size is calculated before the analysis, with the assumptions shown
The metric and the guardrail metric are both defined up front
The result states the confidence interval and what you would ship

Business intelligence.title: Build a report a manager would actually use
Business intelligence.description: Turn data into a report with definitions that hold up to questioning.
acceptance_criteria: Every metric has a written definition and a source query
The report answers three questions a manager asked for
Refresh steps are documented so someone else can maintain it

Excel.title: Build a model with no hardcoded numbers in formulas
Excel.description: Make a spreadsheet that someone can audit and change safely.
acceptance_criteria: Inputs, calculations and outputs are on separate clearly labelled sheets
Lookups and pivot analysis are used rather than manual copying
A checks sheet flags broken assumptions automatically

Power BI.title: Publish a dashboard with a clean data model
Power BI.description: Build a report where the relationships and measures are deliberate.
acceptance_criteria: The data model uses relationships rather than merged flat tables
At least five DAX measures are written and documented
The report answers a stated business question on the first screen

Tableau.title: Build a dashboard that answers one question well
Tableau.description: Make a focused dashboard rather than a wall of charts.
acceptance_criteria: The dashboard has one headline answer and supporting detail
Filters and interactions are documented
The workbook is published with a short written interpretation

Web scraping.title: Collect a dataset ethically and reliably
Web scraping.description: Build a scraper that respects the site and survives small changes.
acceptance_criteria: robots.txt and rate limits are respected and the code shows it
Data is written to a structured file with a documented schema
The scraper handles missing fields without crashing

JavaScript.title: Build a feature without a framework
JavaScript.description: Prove you know the language underneath the library.
acceptance_criteria: The feature uses modules, async code and DOM events with no framework
Errors and loading states are handled explicitly
The README explains one thing you had to reason about, such as the event loop

TypeScript.title: Add types to an existing JavaScript project
TypeScript.description: Migrate real code and let the types find real bugs.
acceptance_criteria: strict mode is on and there are no any types left in the migrated code
Shared types live in one place and are reused, not duplicated
The README lists two bugs the types exposed

HTML.title: Build a page that is correct without CSS
HTML.description: Structure content properly before styling it.
acceptance_criteria: The page uses landmarks, headings in order and real form labels
It validates with no errors
It is usable and readable with stylesheets disabled, shown by a screenshot

CSS.title: Rebuild a layout with modern CSS only
CSS.description: Use grid and flexbox deliberately instead of reaching for a framework.
acceptance_criteria: The layout works from 360px to 1440px with no horizontal scroll
Spacing and colour come from custom properties, not repeated values
The README explains one layout decision and the alternative you rejected

React.title: Build a feature with real state, not a tutorial clone
React.description: Handle the states a real feature has: loading, empty, error, success.
acceptance_criteria: All four states are implemented and reachable in the UI
State lives at the right level and the README explains the choice
One component is covered by tests through its rendered behaviour

Next.js.title: Ship an app that renders on the server where it should
Next.js.description: Use server and client components deliberately and be able to defend it.
acceptance_criteria: At least one route fetches data on the server and renders without client JS
Loading and error states use the framework's own conventions
The README explains which components are client side and why

Redux.title: Manage state that genuinely needs managing
Redux.description: Introduce a store for state that is actually shared, not for everything.
acceptance_criteria: The store holds only state shared across routes or components
Async flows handle pending, fulfilled and rejected states
The README argues why local state was not enough

Tailwind CSS.title: Build a themed interface with design tokens
Tailwind CSS.description: Use a configured theme rather than scattering arbitrary values.
acceptance_criteria: Colours, spacing and type come from the config, not arbitrary classes
Dark mode works and is tested at both themes
Repeated patterns are extracted into components, not copied classes

Web performance.title: Make one page measurably faster
Web performance.description: Profile first, fix second, and show the numbers.
acceptance_criteria: A Lighthouse report before and after is committed
Largest Contentful Paint improves and the cause of the improvement is named
JavaScript bundle size before and after is recorded

Accessibility.title: Fix the accessibility of a page you built
Accessibility.description: Audit a real page and repair what the audit finds.
acceptance_criteria: Every interactive element is reachable and operable by keyboard
Colour contrast meets AA and the check is shown
The page is navigated with a screen reader and the notes are in the README

Responsive design.title: Make one interface work from 360px up
Responsive design.description: Design for the small screen first and let it grow.
acceptance_criteria: No horizontal scrolling at 360px, shown by screenshots
Touch targets are at least 44px and spacing adapts by breakpoint
The README shows the same screen at three widths

Node.js.title: Build a service that handles failure well
Node.js.description: Write a Node service that behaves under bad input and downstream errors.
acceptance_criteria: Input is validated at the boundary with a consistent error response
Unhandled rejections and timeouts are handled explicitly
The service shuts down cleanly on SIGTERM

Express.title: Build an API with real middleware
Express.description: Structure an Express app so routes stay thin.
acceptance_criteria: Validation, authentication and error handling are middleware, not inline code
Routes contain no business logic, which lives in a service layer
Errors return a consistent JSON shape with correct status codes

Django.title: Build a Django app with tests and migrations
Django.description: Use the framework properly rather than fighting it.
acceptance_criteria: Models, migrations and the admin are all used
Views are covered by tests using the test client
Settings are environment aware with no secrets in code

Flask.title: Build a small Flask service with structure
Flask.description: Keep a Flask app organised past the single file stage.
acceptance_criteria: Blueprints separate concerns and the app factory pattern is used
Configuration comes from the environment
Every route has a test

FastAPI.title: Build a typed API with automatic documentation
FastAPI.description: Use the framework's typing to get validation and docs for free.
acceptance_criteria: Request and response models are declared with Pydantic
The generated OpenAPI docs are shown in the README
One dependency, such as authentication, is injected rather than imported

Java.title: Build a small Java service with tests
Java.description: Write idiomatic Java with a build tool and a test suite.
acceptance_criteria: The project builds with Maven or Gradle in one command
JUnit tests cover the core logic
Collections and streams are used where they fit, with a note on the choice

Spring Boot.title: Build a REST service with Spring Boot
Spring Boot.description: Use dependency injection and the framework's testing support properly.
acceptance_criteria: Controller, service and repository layers are separated
Integration tests run against an in memory or containerised database
Configuration is externalised in application properties

Git.title: Clean up a repository history and workflow
Git.description: Show you can use Git deliberately, not only commit and push.
acceptance_criteria: The repository uses branches and pull requests with reviewable commits
Commit messages follow a convention and explain why, not what
The README documents the branching workflow you chose

Data structures and algorithms.title: Publish solutions with your reasoning
Data structures and algorithms.description: Solve problems and explain the thinking, since that is what interviews test.
acceptance_criteria: Thirty solutions grouped by pattern, each with a complexity note
Each file explains the approach in three lines before the code
Five problems include a brute force and an optimised version side by side

GraphQL.title: Build a schema that avoids the N plus one problem
GraphQL.description: Design a GraphQL API and make it efficient.
acceptance_criteria: The schema has types, queries and at least one mutation
Batching or data loading is used and the query count is shown before and after
Errors are returned in a way clients can act on

Vite.title: Set up and tune a build for a real project
Vite.description: Understand your build tool rather than inheriting a template.
acceptance_criteria: The config handles environment variables and aliases deliberately
Production build size is reported before and after one optimisation
The README explains what the build actually does

Figma.title: Translate a design into a faithful interface
Figma.description: Work from a design file the way you would on a team.
acceptance_criteria: Spacing, type and colour match the design and the deviations are listed
Component states from the file are all implemented
The README links the frames you built from

Postman.title: Document and test an API collection
Postman.description: Make your API easy for someone else to try.
acceptance_criteria: A collection covers every endpoint with example requests
Tests assert status codes and response shape
Environment variables keep secrets out of the exported collection

Matplotlib.title: Produce report quality figures from code
Matplotlib.description: Make charts that could go into a report without editing.
acceptance_criteria: Figures are generated by a script, not by hand
Labels, units and legends are complete on every figure
A consistent style is applied across all figures

Agile.title: Run one project with a visible board and honest estimates
Agile.description: Practise the process, not only the code.
acceptance_criteria: Work is broken into issues with acceptance criteria before coding
A board shows the flow and the README links it
The retrospective notes what your estimates got wrong
